title: [Editor] Background plugin gate reads Player Settings symbols while the bridges compile from effective defines
body:
## Summary
TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate decides whether the iOS/Android background plugins are included from the Player Settings define symbols. The managed bridges compile from the effective defines, which can also come from asmdef versionDefines or other sources. The two can disagree, giving a player whose managed bridge calls into a plugin that was excluded, or the reverse.

## Location
- `Editor/TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate.cs:97`

## Problem
ShouldIncludeInBuild reads PlayerSettings.GetScriptingDefineSymbolsForGroup for the active build target (95-99). The managed side is selected by #if TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING at compile time (BackgroundExecutionBridgeFactory.cs:13-19, IosBackgroundTaskBindings.cs:67-91, AndroidBackgroundPluginJni.cs:67-83, AndroidAppPauseListener.cs:1). The class remark (16-20) and PlatformNotes.md:161-163 admit that BuildPlayerOptions.extraScriptingDefines is not seen. The plugin .meta files also carry defineConstraints that the remark says Unity 2021.3 ignores for native plugins, so two mechanisms express one rule.

**Failure scenario.** A CI build script passes the define through extraScriptingDefines (or a newer editor's per-profile defines): the managed bridges compile with DllImport("__Internal") entries and JNI calls, the .mm and the .androidlib are excluded. On iOS the Xcode link fails with undefined turbohttp_* symbols; on Android the class lookup throws, is swallowed (AndroidBackgroundWorkBridge.cs:102-106) and requests silently keep foreground semantics while the app believes background networking is on. Depends on the build pipeline in use; not reproducible statically.

## Suggested fix
Fail the build in OnPreprocessBuild when the compiled player assembly was built with the define but the gate would exclude the plugins (for example by checking a constant emitted under the define via reflection on the built TurboHTTP.Unity assembly), and log once at runtime when the Android plugin class is missing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A build with the background define compiled but the gate excluding the plugins fails in OnPreprocessBuild with a message naming both sides
- [ ] The gate and the managed bridge derive their decision from the same source, or a mismatch is detected and reported at build time
- [ ] The Android managed side logs once at runtime when the plugin class is missing instead of failing silently
- [ ] An Editor test under Tests/Editor/ covers the disagreeing-defines case and fails before the fix

title: [Mobile] Android deferred-work WorkManager job returns Result.retry() forever and is never cancelled after the process dies
body:
## Summary
TurboHttpBackgroundWorker returns Result.retry() unconditionally, so every queued deferred-work request leaves a WorkManager job that is rescheduled indefinitely. Nothing cancels these jobs after the process dies, and CancelDeferredWork returns early when the plugin is not initialized. Orphaned jobs keep waking the app and draining battery for every user of the Android background bridge.

## Location
- `Plugins/Android/TurboHttpBackground.androidlib/src/main/java/com/turbohttp/background/TurboHttpBackgroundWorker.java:24`

## Problem
TurboHttpBackgroundWorker.doWork (lines 21-25) always returns Result.retry(). TurboHttpBackgroundPlugin.enqueueDeferredWork (TurboHttpBackgroundPlugin.java:52-58) enqueues a OneTimeWorkRequest with no constraints, no attempt cap and ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP. The only cancel is cancelDeferredWork (java:63-76), reached from AndroidBackgroundWorkBridge.TryMarkReplayComplete (Runtime/Unity/Mobile/Android/AndroidBackgroundWorkBridge.cs:246-266), which only BackgroundNetworkingInterceptor.TryDequeueReplayable calls (Runtime/Unity/Mobile/BackgroundNetworkingInterceptor.cs:51-68). Both the replay queue (BoundedRequestQueue, BackgroundNetworkingInterceptor.cs:222-272) and _queuedWorkIds (AndroidBackgroundWorkBridge.cs:34) are in-memory, so a new process knows no keys; AndroidBackgroundPluginJni.CancelDeferredWork (AndroidBackgroundPluginJni.cs:133-140) is also a no-op until EnsureInitialized ran in that process. The worker comment says the host app can 'rehydrate its policy and state', but no managed API lists or restores persisted work. No test covers a process restart; Documentation~/PlatformNotes.md:147-158 does not mention it. WorkManager's merged manifest adds RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED, so the jobs are rescheduled after reboot too.

**Failure scenario.** App built with TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING and UseBackgroundNetworking() is paused for more than 5 s with a GET in flight: the request is queued and enqueueUniqueWork persists a job. The OS then kills the paused process (the normal outcome). WorkManager starts the app process to run the worker, which returns retry; the backoff grows to the 5 h cap and the cycle continues across reboots indefinitely. Every distinct dedupe key (by default every distinct URL) adds another job; a later process cannot cancel them because it does not know the keys.

## Suggested fix
Give the placeholder a terminal state: return success/failure after one run (or cap on getRunAttemptCount), tag all work and cancel by tag at startup (cancelAllWorkByTag) so a cold start clears orphans, and make CancelDeferredWork initialize the plugin instead of returning early. Until a cold-started process can actually replay, do not enqueue persistent work at all.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The worker returns a terminal result (success or failure) after one run or after a capped getRunAttemptCount
- [ ] All deferred work is tagged and cancelAllWorkByTag runs at startup so a cold start clears orphans
- [ ] CancelDeferredWork initializes the plugin instead of returning early
- [ ] Validated on an Android device or emulator and recorded: no job remains enqueued after the process is killed and the app restarted

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-protocol-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. TurboHttpBackgroundWorker.java:21-25 returns Result.retry() unconditionally; TurboHttpBackgroundPlugin.java:52-58 enqueues an unconstrained OneTimeWorkRequest with ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP and no attempt cap or tag. The only cancel path is cancelUniqueWork (java:63-76) <- AndroidBackgroundWorkBridge.TryMarkReplayComplete (AndroidBackgroundWorkBridge.cs:246-266) <- BackgroundNetworkingInterceptor.TryDequeueReplayable (BackgroundNetworkingInterceptor.cs:51-68), which nothing in Runtime/ calls (tests only) and Documentation~ never mentions, so even a live process leaves the job retrying unless the app calls that API. Replay queue (cs:222-272) and _queuedWorkIds (bridge cs:34) are in-memory, and AndroidBackgroundPluginJni.CancelDeferredWork (cs:133-140) returns early before EnsureInitialized, so a new process can neither know nor cancel the keys. No guard found. #266 covers device validation of begin/end/expiry only; #267 (closed) introduced the enqueue. Mitigation: feature is experimental and opt-in (TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING); WorkManager retry cadence/boot persistence is platform behaviour not run here.

Also reported as `unity-design-18`, `unity-runtime-18` (merged into this issue).

Related: #266.

title: [Unity] JsonUtilitySerializer passes untrusted JSON to JsonUtility.FromJson without depth bound or BOM handling
body:
## Summary
JsonUtilitySerializer hands response bodies directly to JsonUtility.FromJson. Unlike LiteJson it applies no nesting depth limit and no BOM handling, and JsonUtility.ToJson can emit non-JSON number tokens such as NaN or Infinity. Peer-controlled deeply nested JSON can exhaust the stack or memory, and invalid JSON can be written on the request path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Bootstrap/JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:268`

## Problem
For every custom [Serializable] type DeserializeValue calls JsonUtility.FromJson(json, target) directly (lines 258-268); MaxDepth = 64 (line 63) only counts this class's own array recursion. The built-in path goes through LiteJson, whose reader enforces MaxDepth 64 and ignores one leading U+FEFF (Runtime/JSON/LiteJson/JsonReader.cs:23, 49, 89-90). Deserialize<T>(ReadOnlySequence<byte>) keeps a BOM in the decoded string (lines 153-169). SerializeValue returns JsonUtility.ToJson(value) unchanged (197), which writes NaN/Infinity for non-finite float fields. HasSerializableFields also admits [SerializeReference] fields (366-369), for which JsonUtility lets the JSON name the concrete type. This serializer is installed as the default at startup (TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:87-91).

**Failure scenario.** response.AsJson<Dictionary<string, object>>() accepts a body that starts with a UTF-8 BOM while AsJson<MyDto>() on the same body fails; a hostile server can send megabytes of nested '{"a":' to the native parser with no managed depth check (confirm on device whether Unity's parser is recursion-safe); WithJsonBody(dto) with a NaN field sends a body that is not JSON.

## Spec reference
RFC 8259 sections 6, 8.1 and 9

## Suggested fix
Before JsonUtility.FromJson strip one leading U+FEFF and run a cheap depth/shape scan with the same limit as LiteJson; reject or map non-finite numbers on the write path; document or refuse [SerializeReference] DTOs for untrusted input.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One leading U+FEFF is stripped before FromJson
- [ ] A depth/shape scan with the same limit as LiteJson runs before FromJson and rejects over-deep input with the documented error
- [ ] Non-finite numbers on the write path are rejected or mapped
- [ ] A test under Tests/Runtime/Json/ fails before the fix for deep nesting and BOM input

title: [JSON] JsonUtilitySerializer parses a top-level array three times and copies the JSON bytes an extra time
body:
## Summary
For a top-level array, JsonUtilitySerializer scans and parses the payload three times and copies the bytes once more in each direction. This adds CPU and allocations per JSON response and request on mobile.

## Location
- `Runtime/Bootstrap/JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:298`

## Problem
DeserializeArray parses the whole text into a List<object> tree with LiteJson (273), then for each element serializes the tree back to a string (298) and parses that string again with JsonUtility.FromJson through DeserializeValue (299, 268). Serialize<T>(T, IBufferWriter<byte>) builds the string, encodes it into a new byte[] and copies that into the writer (143-146). Deserialize<T>(ReadOnlySequence<byte>) copies the sequence into a rented array before decoding, also for a single segment (155-162). The bootstrap installs this serializer as the default (TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:87-91).

**Failure scenario.** 'AsJson<Item[]>()' on a 1 MB top-level array of 5000 objects, the common REST list shape -> a boxed dictionary tree for the whole document, 5000 intermediate strings and a third parse: several times the document size in garbage and about three parses of CPU on the default path.

## Suggested fix
Split the top-level array into element substrings with a small depth-tracking scanner and pass each to JsonUtility.FromJson; encode with Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(string, Span<byte>) straight into the writer and decode single-segment input from its span.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Top-level arrays are split into element substrings by one depth-tracking scan and each element is parsed once
- [ ] Encoding writes UTF-8 directly into the writer and single-segment input is decoded from its span
- [ ] Allocations and copies per call are measured before and after, with the target of one parse and no intermediate byte[] copy
- [ ] A test under Tests/Runtime/Json/ asserts identical results for arrays of objects

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-runtime-26` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Runtime/Bootstrap/JsonUtilitySerializer.cs: DeserializeArray parses the whole text into a LiteJson object tree (:273), re-serializes every element to a string (:298) and parses it again via DeserializeValue -> JsonUtility.FromJson (:299, :268). Serialize<T>(T, IBufferWriter<byte>) goes string -> new byte[] -> CopyTo writer (:143-146); Deserialize<T>(ReadOnlySequence<byte>) always copies into a rented array before GetString, single segment included (:155-162). Installed as the process default by TurboHttpBootstrap.RegisterJsonBridge (TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:87-91) unless a custom serializer exists. No guard or fast path found. Cost is confined to top-level T[] of [Serializable] types (scalars and Dictionary/List<object> take the LiteJson path at :108-109), which JsonUtility cannot parse natively, so this is a workaround with avoidable 3x parse plus per-element strings, not a correctness defect.

title: [Unity] WebSocket UniTask adapters use Task.AsUniTask() and fail on worker threads without a SynchronizationContext
body:
## Summary
The WebSocket UniTask extensions convert with Task.AsUniTask(), which needs a current SynchronizationContext. Called from a worker thread it fails, while the HTTP adapters avoid this with a private async UniTask wrapper. Users awaiting WebSocket operations off the main thread get exceptions.

## Location
- `Runtime/UniTask.WebSocket/WebSocketUniTaskExtensions.cs:26`

## Problem
ConnectAsUniTask (two overloads), SendAsUniTask (three overloads) and CloseAsUniTask return client.XxxAsync(...).AsUniTask() (26, 37, 46, 55, 64, 82). UniTask's Task.AsUniTask defaults to useCurrentSynchronizationContext: true and schedules through TaskScheduler.FromCurrentSynchronizationContext(), which throws InvalidOperationException when SynchronizationContext.Current is null. The HTTP adapter file records this: 'Task.AsUniTask() throws without a SynchronizationContext, so both paths await here instead' (UHttpClientUniTaskExtensions.cs:192-193). No test covers the WebSocket adapters (no ConnectAsUniTask or SendAsUniTask under Tests). UniTask itself is not in the checkout, so the throw is taken from the in-repo comment and the library's known behaviour.

**Failure scenario.** 'await UniTask.SwitchToThreadPool(); await socket.SendAsUniTask(data);', or a send issued from a continuation that resumed on the thread pool -> InvalidOperationException from the adapter instead of a send. Confirm with a test that calls SendAsUniTask inside Task.Run.

## Suggested fix
Wrap the Task in a private 'async UniTask' awaiter as the HTTP adapters and ReceiveAsUniTask already do, and add a worker-thread test for each adapter.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every WebSocket UniTask adapter wraps the Task in a private async UniTask awaiter like the HTTP adapters
- [ ] Each adapter works when called from a thread-pool thread
- [ ] A worker-thread test per adapter under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-runtime-20` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: platform-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Runtime/UniTask.WebSocket/WebSocketUniTaskExtensions.cs:26,37,46,55,64,82 return client.XxxAsync(...).AsUniTask() on Task-returning methods (IWebSocketClient.cs:63-84 are Task, only ReceiveAsync is ValueTask and goes through the private async awaiter at :94-102). UniTask's Task.AsUniTask(useCurrentSynchronizationContext: true) builds the continuation with TaskScheduler.FromCurrentSynchronizationContext(), which throws InvalidOperationException when SynchronizationContext.Current is null; the sibling HTTP adapter states this and avoids it (Runtime/UniTask/UHttpClientUniTaskExtensions.cs:192-193). UniTask source is not in the checkout (pinned fetch only, #311 closed), so the throw rests on the in-repo comment plus the library's known source. No guard: no test references ConnectAsUniTask/SendAsUniTask/CloseAsUniTask (Tests/Runtime/UniTask has only UniTaskCancellationTests for HTTP). Worse than reported: the underlying ConnectAsync/SendAsync/CloseAsync is invoked before AsUniTask throws, so the send starts, the caller gets an exception and the Task is left unobserved (a retry double-sends).

Also reported as `unity-design-24`, `unity-protocol-15` (merged into this issue).

Related: [[R11-unity-design-25]].

title: [Packaging] UniTask adapter assemblies are not autoReferenced and are absent when UniTask is not the com.cysharp.unitask package
body:
## Summary
The two UniTask adapter assemblies are not autoReferenced, so projects without their own asmdef cannot use them. They also compile only when the UniTask package define is set, which does not happen for UniTask installed from source or another package name. Users see the adapters silently missing.

## Location
- `Runtime/UniTask/TurboHTTP.UniTask.asmdef:13`

## Problem
Both UniTask asmdefs set autoReferenced false (TurboHTTP.UniTask.asmdef:13, TurboHTTP.UniTask.WebSocket.asmdef:14) while every other user-facing module is auto-referenced; README.md:154 and QuickStart.md:10 tell users that scripts without an asmdef see the modules automatically. The define comes only from versionDefines on the package name com.cysharp.unitask (17-23) and is also a defineConstraint (14-16) and an #if around every file. Documentation~/Modules/UniTask.md:7 documents the explicit reference but not the manual define.

**Failure scenario.** A project whose scripts live in Assembly-CSharp installs UniTask and writes using TurboHTTP.UniTask: CS0246, and Assembly-CSharp cannot add a reference. A project that imported UniTask from the .unitypackage (a supported UniTask install route, same 'UniTask' asmdef) never gets TURBOHTTP_UNITASK defined, so the adapter assemblies are skipped without any message.

## Suggested fix
Make the two assemblies autoReferenced (they only compile when the define is set, so there is no cost otherwise) and document adding TURBOHTTP_UNITASK to Scripting Define Symbols for non-UPM UniTask installs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both UniTask asmdefs are autoReferenced and still compile to nothing without the define
- [ ] Documentation states how to add TURBOHTTP_UNITASK to Scripting Define Symbols for non-UPM UniTask installs
- [ ] A project without its own asmdef can call the adapters after the documented setup, verified in a sample or Editor test

title: [Unity] HTTP UniTask adapters honour playerLoopTiming only when it is not Update and their summaries claim zero overhead
body:
## Summary
The HTTP UniTask adapters switch to the requested PlayerLoopTiming only when it is not Update, so an explicit Update request does not move the continuation to the main thread. The XML summaries claim zero overhead, which is not accurate. Callers cannot predict which thread continues.

## Location
- `Runtime/UniTask/UHttpClientUniTaskExtensions.cs:199`

## Problem
AwaitResponse awaits the ValueTask and returns at once when playerLoopTiming == PlayerLoopTiming.Update (198-200); any other timing yields onto the player loop (204). The await resumes through the captured SynchronizationContext, which exists only when the call started on the main thread. Documentation~/Modules/UniTask.md says continuations 'resume on the main thread' and that DefaultPlayerLoopTiming 'selects the player-loop timing used for continuations'. Every wrapper is summarised as 'Zero-overhead UniTask wrapper' (15, 28, 41, ...) although each call goes through an async UniTask state machine.

**Failure scenario.** A caller on a worker thread (after UniTask.SwitchToThreadPool) awaits client.GetAsync(url) with the default timing and touches a Unity object in the continuation: it runs on a thread-pool thread and Unity throws. The same code with PlayerLoopTiming.LastUpdate runs on the main thread.

## Suggested fix
Decide one contract: either always switch to the requested timing unless already on the main thread, or document that Update means 'no switch' and rename the parameter accordingly. Fix the summaries.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One contract is chosen: always switch to the requested timing unless already on the main thread, or document that Update means no switch and rename the parameter
- [ ] XML summaries are corrected to match the behaviour
- [ ] A test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ asserts the thread of the continuation for each timing value

title: [WebSocket] Unity bridge discovers reconnect events by casting to ResilientWebSocketClient and UnityWebSocketClient cannot set headers, TLS backend or proxy
body:
## Summary
UnityWebSocketBridge finds reconnect events by casting to the concrete ResilientWebSocketClient, so any other client type loses them. The MonoBehaviour UnityWebSocketClient also exposes no way to set headers, TLS backend or proxy. Unity users cannot configure authenticated or proxied WebSocket connections.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:56`

## Problem
The constructor does client as ResilientWebSocketClient and subscribes OnReconnecting/OnReconnected only on that type (56, 65-69); the events are not on IWebSocketClient (Runtime/WebSocket/IWebSocketClient.cs:14-48). UnityWebSocketClient.BuildConnectionOptions sets only ping interval, one sub-protocol, the default reconnect policy and AllowCleartext (UnityWebSocketClient.cs:560-584); the only hook to change the client or its options is the internal test seam ClientFactory (87). Every close, including an explicit DisconnectAsync or a pause, sends the reason 'Unity component disabled.' (500-503).

**Failure scenario.** A decorator around a resilient client (logging wrapper, test double, a second bridge) silently loses OnReconnecting/OnReconnected. A scene component cannot connect to an endpoint that needs an Authorization header or a cookie, or go through a proxy, so the component is unusable for authenticated services and users must drop to the bridge API.

## Suggested fix
Put the reconnect events on an interface in TurboHTTP.WebSocket that the bridge probes, and give UnityWebSocketClient a public options callback (or serialized headers plus a ConfigureOptions event) and a neutral close reason.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reconnect events live on an interface in TurboHTTP.WebSocket that the bridge probes instead of a concrete cast
- [ ] UnityWebSocketClient exposes an options callback (or serialized headers plus ConfigureOptions event) covering headers, TLS backend and proxy
- [ ] A neutral close reason type is used on the Unity-facing API
- [ ] A test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ covers a non-resilient client and configured options

title: [Unity] WebSocket bridge callbacks raised on the main thread run inline and overtake already-queued messages
body:
## Summary
When a bridge callback is raised on the main thread it executes inline instead of being queued, so it can run before messages already waiting in the dispatcher. This breaks the documented ordering of lifecycle events relative to messages, for example OnClose before the last OnMessage.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:327`

## Problem
DispatchCore calls MainThreadDispatcher.ExecuteAsync(item.RunAction) (line 327). With the default AllowInlineExecutionOnMainThread = true, ExecuteAsync runs the action immediately when the caller is the main thread (Runtime/Unity/MainThreadDispatcher.cs:352-364) instead of enqueueing behind the user queue. DispatchLifecycle's contract says a lifecycle callback 'takes the user lane so it stays ordered after the messages already queued' (308-313), and UnityWebSocketClient.ReleaseConnectionAsync relies on the fallback disconnect being 'queued behind the close event the client raised' (Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketClient.cs:552-557). WebSocketClient.CloseAsync raises OnClosed on the calling thread when its awaits complete synchronously (Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClient.cs:313-327).

**Failure scenario.** The peer closes; messages and the client's close event are in the dispatcher queue. In the same frame game code on the main thread calls Connect() or Disconnect() on the stale connection and the release path completes synchronously: OnDisconnectedEvent fires inline with the fallback code (1006 or 1001) before the queued messages and the real close code, which TryMarkDisconnected then discards; OnMessageReceivedEvent callbacks arrive after the disconnect event.

## Suggested fix
Dispatch bridge callbacks through an always-queued path (a dispatcher overload that never inlines) so ordering does not depend on the raising thread.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Bridge callbacks always go through a queued path that never inlines, regardless of the raising thread
- [ ] Lifecycle events are delivered after all previously queued messages
- [ ] A test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ raising events from the main thread and a worker thread asserts identical ordering

title: [WebSocket] UnityWebSocketClient copies every binary message a second time before raising OnBinaryReceivedEvent
body:
## Summary
UnityWebSocketClient copies each binary message into a new array before raising OnBinaryReceivedEvent, even when the message already owns an exact-size array. This doubles allocation and copy work for binary traffic on mobile.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketClient.cs:610`

## Problem
WebSocketClient raises OnMessage with WebSocketMessage.CreateDetachedCopy(message), a new exactly-sized byte[] that is not pooled (WebSocketClient.cs:463-475, WebSocketMessage.cs:82-108). HandleMessage then calls message.Data.ToArray() (610) and disposes the detached message (615), which does nothing for a non-pooled buffer.

**Failure scenario.** A stream of 64 KB binary frames at 30 messages per second -> an extra 1.9 MB/s of garbage on top of the copy the core already made.

## Suggested fix
Let a detached message hand over its array (an internal 'take exact buffer' on WebSocketMessage) and copy only when the buffer is pooled or larger than the payload.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A detached message can hand over its exact array and the copy happens only when the buffer is pooled or larger than the payload
- [ ] Copies per binary message drop from two to one (zero extra for exact buffers), measured in a test
- [ ] A test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ asserts payload integrity and no pooled-buffer aliasing

title: [Unity] UHttpClient.WebSocket() copies three client options, ignores the rest including proxy, and leaks the client on failed connect
body:
## Summary
The UHttpClient.WebSocket extension maps only three of the client's options into the handshake and silently ignores others such as proxy, cleartext policy, TLS backend and timeouts. If ConnectAsync throws, the created bridge is not disposed. It also returns a hidden type and validates arguments only inside an async path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketExtensions.cs:44`

## Problem
BuildWebSocketOptions (44-54) copies TlsBackend, AllowCleartext and DefaultHeaders from client.GetOptionsSnapshot(). UHttpClientOptions.Proxy (Runtime/Core/UHttpClientOptions.cs:76) is not mapped to WebSocketConnectionOptions.ProxySettings (Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:115), nor are timeouts. WebSocket(Uri) creates the bridge and client and awaits ConnectAsync without try/finally (38-41), unlike UnityWebSocketClient which disposes on failure (UnityWebSocketClient.cs:404-409). The return type is Task<IWebSocketClient>, so ReceiveAsCoroutine, OnMessageDropped, OnReconnecting/OnReconnected need a downcast. The Uri overload is async, so a null client faults the task while the string overload validates the URL synchronously (19-23, 33-36); neither method has XML docs.

**Failure scenario.** An app configured with options.Proxy (corporate network, or a privacy proxy) calls client.WebSocket("wss://..."): the WebSocket connects directly, bypassing the proxy the HTTP requests of the same client use, and fails where direct egress is blocked. Each failed connect leaves an undisposed WebSocketClient behind.

## Suggested fix
Map every option that has a WebSocket counterpart (proxy, cleartext, TLS backend, DNS/connect timeouts) or accept an Action<WebSocketConnectionOptions> so the caller sees what is applied; dispose the bridge when ConnectAsync throws; return UnityWebSocketBridge; validate arguments synchronously in a non-async wrapper.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every client option with a WebSocket counterpart is mapped, or an Action<WebSocketConnectionOptions> shows what is applied
- [ ] The bridge is disposed when ConnectAsync throws
- [ ] The public return type is UnityWebSocketBridge and argument validation is synchronous
- [ ] A test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ asserts mapped options and disposal on connect failure

title: [Auth] client.WebSocket() copies default headers including credentials into the handshake but drops proxy settings
body:
## Summary
The UHttpClient.WebSocket extension copies all of the client's default headers, including Authorization and cookies, into the WebSocket handshake, and it does not carry over the client's proxy settings. This disagrees with the documented inheritance, can send credentials to a different origin than intended, and bypasses a required proxy.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketExtensions.cs:51`

## Problem
BuildWebSocketOptions (lines 44-54) sets TlsBackend, AllowCleartext and CustomHeaders = clientOptions.DefaultHeaders.Clone(); it does not map UHttpClientOptions.Proxy (Runtime/Core/UHttpClientOptions.cs:76) to WebSocketConnectionOptions.ProxySettings, which stays WebSocketProxySettings.None (Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:115; RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:84 uses it as is). WebSocketHandshake.BuildRequest writes every custom header to the target and throws ArgumentException for Host/Connection/Upgrade (Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketHandshake.cs:55-64, 129-147). Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:20 says the socket 'inherits the TLS backend and cleartext setting of the HTTP client' only.

**Failure scenario.** A client is configured with DefaultHeaders Authorization: Bearer <api token> and Proxy = http://corp-proxy:3128. httpClient.WebSocket("wss://realtime.thirdparty.example/feed") sends the bearer token to the third-party host and connects to it directly, bypassing the proxy the HTTP requests use (it fails outright on a proxy-only network). A client whose DefaultHeaders contain Connection: keep-alive makes every client.WebSocket call throw ArgumentException.

## Suggested fix
Map ProxySettings (address, credentials, bypass list) into WebSocketProxySettings, and copy only an allow-list of default headers (User-Agent and similar) or skip credential and hop-by-hop/reserved headers; document exactly what is inherited.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ProxySettings (address, credentials, bypass list) map into WebSocketProxySettings
- [ ] Only an allow-list of default headers is copied; credential and hop-by-hop or reserved headers are skipped
- [ ] Documentation lists exactly what is inherited
- [ ] A test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ asserts credentials are not copied and the proxy is applied; it fails before the fix

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code as described: BuildWebSocketOptions (UnityWebSocketExtensions.cs:44-54) copies TlsBackend, AllowCleartext and DefaultHeaders.Clone() only; UHttpClientOptions.Proxy (UHttpClientOptions.cs:76) is not mapped, so WebSocketConnectionOptions.ProxySettings stays None (WebSocketConnectionOptions.cs:115). WebSocketHandshake writes every custom header and throws ArgumentException for reserved names such as Connection/Host (WebSocketHandshake.cs:54-64, 129-147). No test covers client.WebSocket inheritance. Proxy drop and the reserved-header throw are real. The credential sub-claim is weaker than stated: DefaultHeaders are sent to every host by the HTTP client as well (UHttpClient.cs:182), so sending them on the handshake matches existing semantics; the defect there is that Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:20 lists only TLS backend and cleartext as inherited.

title: [Unity] UnityWebSocketReceiveCoroutine.ReceiveAsCoroutine ends silently on a receive failure when no onError callback is passed
body:
## Summary
ReceiveAsCoroutine stops the coroutine when the receive task faults and no onError callback was supplied, without logging anything. The HTTP coroutine wrapper logs such faults. Unity developers using the coroutine receive helper see the connection stop with no trace.

Log the exception when _onError is null, as the HTTP coroutine wrapper does.

title: [Unity] AudioClipHandler runs a synchronous recursive temp-directory sweep with file deletes on the main thread at player start
body:
## Summary
At every player start the audio pipeline sweeps its temp directory recursively and deletes files synchronously on the main thread before the first scene loads. A large leftover directory delays startup. Every game using the audio pipeline pays this cost.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/AudioClipHandler.cs:126`

## Problem
AudioClipHandler.RuntimeInitialize (RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod BeforeSceneLoad, 123-127) calls UnityTempFileManager.EnsureStartupSweep, which runs Directory.Exists, Directory.GetFiles(root, prefix, AllDirectories) over the shard directories and File.Delete per file inline (UnityTempFileManager.cs:166-191). It runs whether or not the project uses audio. Streamed clips leave their files for this sweep by design (StreamedAudioTempFiles.cs:40-41), up to MaxActiveTempFiles = 128 files of at least 2 MB each.

**Failure scenario.** An app that streamed many clips in the previous session is cold-started on a phone with slow flash -> the directory walk and up to 128 unlinks run on the main thread during startup and add to time-to-first-frame.

## Suggested fix
Run the sweep on the thread pool (the root path is already cached on the main thread) and skip paths reserved in the current session.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The temp-directory sweep runs on the thread pool and the main thread only caches the root path
- [ ] Paths reserved by the current session are skipped by the sweep
- [ ] Startup main-thread time spent in the sweep is measured and documented as near zero in the PR
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Unity] AudioClipPipelineOptions has no bound on source size or decoded size; clips below 2 MB are fully decompressed in memory
body:
## Summary
The audio pipeline streams only sources above a 2 MB threshold and fully decodes everything below it, with no limit on source bytes or decoded duration. A small compressed file with a very long declared duration decodes into a very large PCM buffer. A hostile server can exhaust memory on the player.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/AudioClipHandler.cs:350`

## Problem
AudioClipPipelineOptions (lines 27-92) has no MaxBodyBytes / max duration / max samples equivalent of TextureOptions. AsAudioClipAsync only rejects an empty body (180-184). DecodeViaUnityTempPathAsync streams only when Body.Length >= StreamingThresholdBytes (default 2 MB, lines 350-352); below that LoadAudioClipCoroutine loads through UnityWebRequestMultimedia with streamAudio = false (418-423), which decompresses the whole clip to PCM. The managed WAV/AIFF decoders are bounded by the body (at most 4x), the Unity path is not.

**Failure scenario.** client.GetAudioClipAsync(url, AudioClipType.OGG) against a hostile or compromised host returns 1.9 MB of near-silent Vorbis at a very low bitrate that declares hours of 44.1 kHz stereo audio. Unity decodes it completely into memory (hundreds of megabytes to gigabytes of PCM) and the app is killed for memory.

## Suggested fix
Add MaxSourceBytes and a decoded-duration/sample bound to AudioClipPipelineOptions with finite defaults; for compressed formats either stream regardless of size or probe the declared duration before a non-streamed load.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AudioClipPipelineOptions exposes MaxSourceBytes and a decoded duration or sample bound with finite defaults, documented with XML docs
- [ ] A source or declared duration above the bound fails with a UHttpException or a documented error instead of allocating the decoded buffer
- [ ] Compressed formats either stream regardless of size or probe the declared duration before decoding
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-protocol-08` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: security.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Code as described: AudioClipPipelineOptions (AudioClipHandler.cs:27-92) has no size/duration bound; AsAudioClipAsync only rejects an empty body (180-184); streaming is chosen only at Body.Length >= StreamingThresholdBytes (350-352, default 2 MB at line 62), otherwise UnityWebRequestMultimedia loads with streamAudio = false (418-423). Source bytes are capped only by the client's 100 MB buffered-body default. The decoded-size blow-up for low-bitrate Vorbis/MP3 happens inside Unity's native decoder and cannot be settled statically. Managed WAV/AIFF decoders are bounded by the body, as the finding says.

title: [Unity] Audio and download-to-file helpers flatten the buffered body into one array and buffer the whole download before writing
body:
## Summary
The audio and file helpers copy the buffered ReadOnlySequence into one contiguous array, and the file helpers hold the entire download in memory before writing it. Large downloads cost memory twice and add large-object-heap allocations on mobile.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/AudioClipHandler.cs:571`

## Problem
AudioClipHandler.GetBodyMemory returns body.ToArray() for a multi-segment body (563-572); it is called for the managed decode (286) and again for the temp-file write when that decode falls back (347). UnityExtensions.ToBodyMemory does the same (UnityExtensions.cs:146-155) after SendBufferedAsync has collected the entire response (127), and PathSafety.WriteAtomicAsync then writes the single array (131-136). Buffered bodies above one 16 KB segment are multi-segment, so the copy is the normal case. Both sinks are files that could be written segment by segment (UnityTempFileManager.WriteBytesAsync 238-259, PathSafety.WriteBytesAsync 228-249).

**Failure scenario.** DownloadToPersistentDataAsync of a 200 MB asset -> 200 MB in pooled segments plus a 200 MB contiguous large-object array before the first byte reaches disk -> out-of-memory on mobile. A 30 MB music track through GetAudioClipAsync allocates one or two extra 30 MB arrays only to copy them into a temp file.

## Suggested fix
Write the ReadOnlySequence segment by segment, and build the download helpers on the streaming response (body source to file) with the SHA-256 computed incrementally; keep the buffered path only for the IntegrityValidator callback.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] File helpers write the ReadOnlySequence segment by segment without flattening
- [ ] Download helpers use the streaming response (body source to file) with SHA-256 computed incrementally; the buffered path remains only for small bodies
- [ ] Peak memory for a download of N MB is measured and stays below N MB plus a fixed buffer
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced, with one correction. AudioClipHandler.GetBodyMemory returns body.ToArray() for multi-segment bodies (AudioClipHandler.cs:563-572) and is called for the managed decode (286) and again for the temp-file write on fallback (347). UnityExtensions.ToBodyMemory does the same (UnityExtensions.cs:146-155) after SendBufferedAsync collected the whole response (127), then PathSafety.WriteAtomicAsync writes the single array (131-136). Buffered bodies are 16 KB-segment sequences (ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:147-222), so the flatten is the normal case, and both sinks are files that could be written per segment (UnityTempFileManager.cs:238-259). Correction: the 200 MB scenario does not run out of memory by default; SendBufferedAsync fails any body above MaxBufferedResponseBodySize = 100 MB with a NetworkError (UHttpClientOptions.cs:107-123), so the 'download to file' helpers cannot fetch files over 100 MB at all unless the cap is raised, and below the cap they hold the body twice (pooled segments + one contiguous large array). Both consequences come from building a file download on the buffered API.

title: [Unity] CoroutineWrapper swallows exceptions thrown by the onSuccess callback
body:
## Summary
An exception thrown in the user's onSuccess callback is routed through the terminal-state gate and discarded. The developer gets no log and no stack trace. Any app with a faulty success handler fails silently.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/CoroutineWrapper.cs:223`

## Problem
In RunTaskCoroutine the success path calls TryEnterTerminal() (line 213) and then onSuccess (218) inside a try whose catch calls InvokeError (221-224). InvokeError starts with 'if (!TryEnterTerminal()) return;' (172-175); the terminal state was already taken on line 213, so the exception is neither passed to onError nor logged. The same applies to GetJsonCoroutine. Tests/Runtime/Unity/CoroutineWrapperTests.cs has no case with a throwing onSuccess.

**Failure scenario.** yield return client.Get(url).SendCoroutine(onSuccess: r => { Parse(r); r.Dispose(); }) where Parse throws NullReferenceException: nothing appears in the console, onError is not called, and the response is never disposed. A plain Unity coroutine would have logged the exception.

## Suggested fix
Do not route callback faults through the terminal-state gate: catch around onSuccess separately and Debug.LogException (or rethrow so Unity logs it), keeping the gate only for choosing between onSuccess and onError.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An exception thrown by onSuccess is logged with Debug.LogException or rethrown so Unity logs it
- [ ] The terminal-state gate still decides only between onSuccess and onError and does not call onError for a callback fault
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-protocol-11` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. RunTaskCoroutine takes the terminal state at CoroutineWrapper.cs:213, calls onSuccess at 218 inside the try; the catch at 221-224 calls InvokeError, whose first statement is if (!TryEnterTerminal()) return (172-175), so the callback's exception is neither forwarded to onError nor logged via Debug.LogException (184-187 unreachable). Same helper serves GetJsonCoroutine (148-154). No throwing-onSuccess case in Tests/Runtime/Unity/CoroutineWrapperTests.cs.

title: [Unity] CoroutineWrapper cleans up only in an iterator finally, so a stopped coroutine neither cancels the request nor disposes the response
body:
## Summary
CoroutineWrapper releases its request, binding and response in a finally block of the iterator. When Unity stops the coroutine the iterator is not resumed, so the request keeps running and the response is not disposed; suppressed completions also leak the response. Pooled response buffers are lost and requests continue after the owner stopped them.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/CoroutineWrapper.cs:226`

## Problem
RunTaskCoroutine disposes lifecycleBinding in a finally (190-229) and SendCoroutineImpl only yields it (113-119). Unity does not dispose a coroutine enumerator when the coroutine is stopped (StopCoroutine, host destroyed or deactivated), which this module already documents for the WebSocket receive coroutine (UnityWebSocketReceiveCoroutine.cs:15-17). With the default callbackOwner = null the binding is not tracked (LifecycleCancellation.cs:138-141), so nothing cancels the request. With an owner that outlives the coroutine host, Poll removes only bindings that are disposed, cancelled or whose owner died (159-190), so ActiveBindings grows without bound. Separately, when the task completed successfully but callbacks are suppressed, the method leaves at 194-195 or 200-201 without disposing task.Result, a UHttpResponse that holds pooled body buffers and the request lease (UHttpResponse.cs:291-325).

**Failure scenario.** A UI panel runs StartCoroutine(request.SendCoroutine(onSuccess)) and is deactivated before the response arrives -> the coroutine stops, the request runs to completion, the UHttpResponse is never disposed (pooled buffers return only through the finalizer, the request lease never completes), the binding's CancellationTokenSource and its registration on the caller's token stay alive, and a later fault is an unobserved task exception. Cancelling the token just as the response completes leaks the response the same way.

## Suggested fix
Move ownership out of the iterator as was done for UnityWebSocketReceiveCoroutine: return a disposable enumerator handle, or attach a continuation to the task that disposes the response and the binding whenever the coroutine did not hand the response to onSuccess. Track owner-less bindings so an abandoned coroutine can be detected.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Stopping the coroutine (StopCoroutine, owner destroyed) cancels the request and disposes the response exactly once
- [ ] A completion suppressed by the terminal gate disposes its response
- [ ] Ownership is moved out of the iterator, for example to a disposable enumerator handle as in UnityWebSocketReceiveCoroutine, or to a task continuation
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-runtime-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: resource-management.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. The binding is disposed only in the iterator finally (CoroutineWrapper.cs:190-229); the module itself documents that Unity never disposes a stopped coroutine's enumerator (UnityWebSocketReceiveCoroutine.cs:15-17, #177), so StopCoroutine / host deactivated or destroyed skips it. With callbackOwner == null the binding is untracked (LifecycleCancellation.cs:138-141), so nothing cancels the request and the completed UHttpResponse is never disposed; UHttpResponse then relies on its finalizer and its own comment says the request lease never completes in that case (Runtime/Core/UHttpResponse.cs:280-282, 309-314). With a live owner, Poll removes only disposed/cancelled/owner-dead bindings (159-190), so abandoned bindings accumulate for the owner's lifetime. Independently, on a successfully completed task the method exits at 200-201 (suppressed) or skips onSuccess at 216-219 without disposing task.Result; also onSuccess == null (218) drops the response undisposed. Existing tests (CoroutineWrapperLifecycleTests.cs) check callback suppression only, not disposal.

title: [Unity] CoroutineWrapper destroyed-owner check is a tautology, so callbacks run for a destroyed owner
body:
## Summary
ShouldInvokeCallbacks compares the owner in a way that is always true for destroyed Unity objects, so callbacks still run after the owner was destroyed and Poll has not yet cancelled. Callbacks then touch destroyed objects and throw.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/CoroutineWrapper.cs:249`

## Problem
ShouldInvokeCallbacks returns 'callbackOwner == null || callbackOwner' (249). callbackOwner is a UnityEngine.Object, so '== null' is Unity's overloaded operator and is true for a destroyed object: the expression is true for null, alive and destroyed owners alike. Suppression therefore depends only on LifecycleCancellation.Poll cancelling the binding from the driver's Update (LifecycleCancellation.cs:153-199, 277-280). Bind has the same confusion: an owner that is already destroyed is treated as no owner and is not tracked (138-141). The lifecycle test passes because it uses Object.Destroy and lets a frame pass, so Poll does the work (CoroutineWrapperLifecycleTests.cs:44-51).

**Failure scenario.** Owner destroyed with DestroyImmediate after the driver's Update in the frame the task completes, or SendCoroutine started with an owner that is already destroyed, or the driver object missing (DontDestroyOnLoad objects cleared; edit-mode coroutines where Update does not tick) -> onSuccess or onError runs against a destroyed MonoBehaviour and user code throws MissingReferenceException.

## Suggested fix
Use 'ReferenceEquals(callbackOwner, null) || callbackOwner' in ShouldInvokeCallbacks, and in Bind tell a null reference from a destroyed object (cancel the binding at once for the latter).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ShouldInvokeCallbacks uses ReferenceEquals(callbackOwner, null) || callbackOwner so a destroyed owner suppresses callbacks
- [ ] Bind distinguishes a null reference from a destroyed object and cancels the binding at once for the latter
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Unity] AiffPcmDecoder accepts AIFF-C files without reading the compression type and decodes them as big-endian PCM
body:
## Summary
The decoder treats AIFC files like plain AIFF and never reads the compressionType field. Little-endian ('sowt'), float and compressed AIFF-C data is decoded as big-endian PCM, producing noise or wrong audio instead of falling back to Unity's decoder.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/Decoders/AiffPcmDecoder.cs:59`

## Problem
ParseAiff accepts FORM type 'AIFC' (lines 58-63) and reads only the first 18 bytes of COMM (87-100); the AIFF-C compressionType at COMM offset 18 ('NONE', 'sowt', 'fl32', 'fl64', 'ulaw', 'alaw', 'ima4') is never inspected. All samples go through ReadPcmSampleBigEndian (146-154). The decode succeeds, so AudioClipHandler.TryManagedDecodeAsync returns the clip and never falls back to Unity's decoder (AudioClipHandler.cs:283-292). No test contains an AIFC payload.

**Failure scenario.** With EnableThreadedDecode = true, a 1 MB .aiff exported by macOS as AIFF-C/sowt (little-endian 16-bit, a common export) is returned as a successfully created AudioClip that plays full-scale noise instead of the audio; without the managed path Unity would have decoded or rejected it.

## Suggested fix
For AIFC read compressionType: decode 'NONE' (and optionally 'sowt' with swapped byte order), throw for every other type so the Unity fallback runs; add AIFC fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AIFC files with compressionType 'NONE' decode correctly; 'sowt' decodes with swapped byte order or is rejected
- [ ] Every other compression type throws so the Unity fallback runs
- [ ] AIFC fixtures for NONE, sowt and an unsupported type are added
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it

The decoder is registered by default (DecoderRegistry.cs:422) and a successful decode returns the clip without Unity fallback (AudioClipHandler.cs:283-292). No AIFC/sowt fixture in Tests. title: [Unity] DecoderRegistry.Initialize silently ignores its configure callback after the registry has bootstrapped
body:
## Summary
Calling Initialize with a configure callback after bootstrap does nothing and gives no signal, while the Register methods throw in the same state. A developer who configures decoders too late gets no decoders and no error.

Throw (as the Register* methods do) or log when Initialize is called with a non-null configure after bootstrap.

title: [Unity] Decoder extension point cannot replace or precede a built-in decoder, and DecoderRoutingPolicy exposes options nothing reads
body:
## Summary
Custom decoders are consulted after the defaults, so they cannot override a built-in decoder, and the builder has no Insert, Remove or Clear. DecoderRoutingPolicy declares concurrency options that no code reads. Users cannot swap in their own decoder and are misled by dead settings.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/Decoders/DecoderRegistry.cs:103`

## Problem
Initialize adds the defaults to the builder first, then earlier Register* calls, then runs configure (102-117); DecoderRegistryBuilder only has AddImageDecoder/AddAudioDecoder (47-59), and resolution returns the first CanDecode match (262-270, 304-312). Registration is sealed by the first resolve (136-137; _bootstrapped and _registrationSealed are always set together, 72-73). GetRoutingPolicy builds a new DecoderRoutingPolicy per resolve (168-235) whose MaxImageDecodeConcurrency/MaxAudioDecodeConcurrency are never read (rg: only assignments), and there is no setter for the policy although the type is public, mutable and has Clone().

## Suggested fix
Resolve custom decoders before defaults (or give the builder Insert/Remove/Clear), delete the unused concurrency fields or wire them to the limiter, and collapse the two sealed flags.

- [ ] Unused concurrency fields on DecoderRoutingPolicy are deleted or wired to the limiter

title: [Unity] 'Threaded' managed audio decode runs synchronously on the caller thread, the Unity main thread when awaited from a MonoBehaviour
body:
## Summary
WavPcmDecoder and the other managed decoders decode synchronously inside DecodeAsync, so awaiting AsAudioClipAsync from a MonoBehaviour decodes on the main thread. Large clips cause frame hitches despite the threaded naming.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/Decoders/WavPcmDecoder.cs:40`

## Problem
WavPcmDecoder.DecodeAsync and AiffPcmDecoder.DecodeAsync return Task.FromResult(Parse(...)) (WavPcmDecoder.cs:35-48, AiffPcmDecoder.cs:35-48): the whole per-sample loop (WavPcmDecoder.cs:126-136) runs before the method returns. AudioClipHandler.TryManagedDecodeAsync awaits it directly with no Task.Run (AudioClipHandler.cs:285-287). AsAudioClipAsync reaches it after 'await limiter.WaitAsync(ct).ConfigureAwait(false)' (192), which completes synchronously when a permit is free, so execution is still on the caller's thread. The option is documented as background threaded decode (47-48) and the interface as a worker-thread decoder contract (IAudioDecoder.cs:7-9).

**Failure scenario.** EnableThreadedDecode = true and a MonoBehaviour does 'var clip = await response.AsAudioClipAsync(AudioClipType.WAV)' on the main thread with a 10 MB 16-bit WAV -> about 5 million samples are converted and a 20 MB float array is allocated on the main thread: the frame hitch the option exists to avoid.

## Suggested fix
Run the managed decode through Task.Run in the handlers (audio and image) so that DecodeAsync never runs on the caller's thread whatever the decoder does.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The audio and image handlers run managed decoding through Task.Run so DecodeAsync never runs on the caller's thread
- [ ] Main-thread time for decoding a large WAV is measured and near zero after the fix
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it and asserts the decoder runs on a thread-pool thread

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-runtime-14` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. WavPcmDecoder.DecodeAsync and AiffPcmDecoder.DecodeAsync are 'return Task.FromResult(Parse(...))' (Decoders/WavPcmDecoder.cs:35-48 with the per-sample loop at 126-136; AiffPcmDecoder.cs:35-48). AudioClipHandler.TryManagedDecodeAsync awaits decoder.DecodeAsync directly, no Task.Run (AudioClipHandler.cs:285-287). AsAudioClipAsync reaches it after 'await limiter.WaitAsync(ct).ConfigureAwait(false)' (192), which completes synchronously when a permit is free, so the decode (and the GetBodyMemory ToArray copy, 563-572) runs on the caller's thread: the main thread when response.AsAudioClipAsync is awaited from a MonoBehaviour. GetAudioClipAsync usually resumes on a pool thread after its own ConfigureAwait(false) (236-239), so it is hit only when the request completes synchronously. The option is documented as background threaded decode (47-48) and the interface as a worker-thread contract (IAudioDecoder.cs:7-9); with the option off the Unity temp-file path does not block the main thread at all, so enabling it makes the main-thread case worse. Opt-in (EnableThreadedDecode default false, body >= 512 KB).

title: [Unity] WAV and AIFF decoders wrap OperationCanceledException in InvalidOperationException, so a cancelled decode falls through to the Unity path
body:
## Summary
The built-in decoders catch every exception including OperationCanceledException and rethrow it as InvalidOperationException. A cancelled decode is logged as a failure and the pipeline then falls back to the Unity decoder, doing work the caller cancelled.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/Decoders/WavPcmDecoder.cs:42`

## Problem
ParseWav/ParseAiff call cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested() inside their loops (WavPcmDecoder.cs:66, 128-129; AiffPcmDecoder.cs:76, 149-150), but DecodeAsync catches Exception and rethrows InvalidOperationException('WAV decode failed at parse stage.') (WavPcmDecoder.cs:42-47, AiffPcmDecoder.cs:42-47). AudioClipHandler.TryManagedDecodeAsync only lets OperationCanceledException through (294-297); anything else logs 'Managed audio decode failed and will fall back to Unity decode path' and returns null (298-304), after which DecodeViaUnityTempPathAsync reserves a temp path before the cancelled token finally stops it in WriteBytesAsync.

**Failure scenario.** A caller cancels a large WAV decode mid-loop: the console shows a decode-failure warning for a healthy file, a temp path is reserved and released, and only then does the operation end as cancelled.

## Suggested fix
Exclude OperationCanceledException from the wrapping catch (catch (Exception ex) when (!(ex is OperationCanceledException))) and return a faulted or cancelled task instead of throwing synchronously from a Task-returning method.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] OperationCanceledException is not wrapped (catch with a when filter) and propagates as cancellation
- [ ] A cancelled decode does not fall through to the Unity decoder and is not logged as a failure
- [ ] DecodeAsync returns a faulted or cancelled task instead of throwing synchronously
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Unity] LifecycleCancellation driver GameObject uses HideAndDontSave and survives the end of play mode in the Editor
body:
## Summary
EnsureDriver creates the '[TurboHTTP LifecycleCancellation]' object with HideFlags.HideAndDontSave plus DontDestroyOnLoad. Objects flagged DontSave are skipped by play-mode exit cleanup, and ResetStaticState only nulls the reference without destroying the object. With domain reload disabled, every play session that uses SendCoroutine or UnityWebSocketClient leaves one hidden driver that keeps polling and cannot be seen or deleted in the Hierarchy.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/LifecycleCancellation.cs:235`

## Problem
EnsureDriver creates '[TurboHTTP LifecycleCancellation]' with hideFlags = HideAndDontSave plus DontDestroyOnLoad (229-238). Objects flagged DontSave are left out of the play-mode exit cleanup. ResetStaticState only nulls _driver (114-125) and does not destroy the previous object. The dispatcher object uses no hide flags (MainThreadDispatcher.cs:697-699) and the Android pause listener uses HideInHierarchy only (AndroidAppPauseListener.cs:16).

**Failure scenario.** Each Editor play session that uses SendCoroutine or UnityWebSocketClient leaves one hidden driver. With domain reload disabled the old drivers keep ticking in later sessions, each running Poll() over all bindings every frame, and they cannot be seen or deleted from the Hierarchy. Confirm with Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll after exiting play mode.

## Suggested fix
Use HideFlags.HideInHierarchy, or destroy the driver on ExitingPlayMode and in ResetStaticState.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The LifecycleCancellation driver is destroyed on exiting play mode and by ResetStaticState, or uses HideFlags.HideInHierarchy so Unity's play-mode cleanup removes it
- [ ] After exiting play mode, Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll finds no '[TurboHTTP LifecycleCancellation]' object

title: [Unity] MainThreadDispatcher settings and UnityWebSocketClient quitting hook are not reset for Enter Play Mode without domain reload
body:
## Summary
MainThreadDispatcher.ResetStaticState does not reset _settings or the queue configuration set by Configure, while TextureDecodeScheduler, AudioClipHandler and UnityTempFileManager reset their options. UnityWebSocketClient.ResetStatics clears _quittingHookRegistered, so EnsureQuittingHook adds another Application.quitting handler each session without removing the earlier one. With domain reload disabled, settings leak into the next session and the Nth quit runs the abort pass N times.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/MainThreadDispatcher.cs:219`

## Problem
MainThreadDispatcher.ResetStaticState resets state, counters and the queue's reject flag but not _settings or the queue configuration set by Configure (218-240; MainThreadWorkQueue.Reset 293-300), while TextureDecodeScheduler, AudioClipHandler and UnityTempFileManager reset their options to defaults. UnityWebSocketClient.ResetStatics clears _quittingHookRegistered (UnityWebSocketClient.cs:114-123), and EnsureQuittingHook then adds HandleApplicationQuitting again without removing the earlier subscription (739-745).

**Failure scenario.** With domain reload disabled, a session that configured UserQueueCapacity = 4 or AllowInlineExecutionOnMainThread = false leaves that in force for the next session while the other modules start from defaults; each play session adds one more quitting handler, so the Nth quit runs the abort pass N times.

## Suggested fix
Reset _settings and reconfigure the queue with defaults in ResetStaticState; subscribe with 'Application.quitting -= h; Application.quitting += h;'.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MainThreadDispatcher.ResetStaticState restores default settings (UserQueueCapacity, AllowInlineExecutionOnMainThread, and the rest) and reconfigures the queue with them
- [ ] UnityWebSocketClient subscribes to Application.quitting at most once per session (unsubscribe before subscribe, or unsubscribe in ResetStatics)
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (configure non-default settings, call ResetStaticState, assert defaults; register the hook twice, assert one handler)

title: [Unity] TurboHTTP.Unity installs a dispatcher GameObject, PlayerLoop system, lowMemory hooks and temp-file sweep in every player unconditionally
body:
## Summary
TurboHTTP.Unity runs several startup hooks regardless of whether a feature is used: the BeforeSceneLoad bootstrap creates a DontDestroyOnLoad dispatcher GameObject and PlayerLoop system, AudioClipHandler triggers a synchronous main-thread temp-file sweep, and TextureDecodeScheduler creates its shared instance and subscribes to lowMemory. The asmdef has no define constraints, so the dispatcher, temp-file manager and scheduler cannot be stripped in any build that links the assembly. Projects that need only part of the module (for example adaptive networking) pay for all of it.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/MainThreadDispatcher.cs:242`

## Problem
MainThreadDispatcher.cs:242-250 [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(BeforeSceneLoad)] always calls EnsureInstanceReady, which creates the '[TurboHTTP MainThreadDispatcher]' GameObject (697-699); Awake installs a PlayerLoop system and an Application.lowMemory handler (280-283). AudioClipHandler.cs:123-127 (BeforeSceneLoad) calls UnityTempFileManager.EnsureStartupSweep, a synchronous Directory.Exists/GetFiles(AllDirectories)/File.Delete on the main thread (UnityTempFileManager.cs:166-191). TextureDecodeScheduler.cs:97-122 forces creation of the Shared instance and subscribes lowMemory. Further SubsystemRegistration hooks: AudioClipHandler.cs:109, DecoderRegistry.cs:75, UnityTempFileManager.cs:108 and 414, LifecycleCancellation.cs:114, StreamedAudioTempFiles.cs:62, MainThreadDispatcher.cs:218 and, on every platform including desktop and iOS, AndroidBackgroundExpirySignal.cs:85 (AndroidAppPauseSource). LifecycleCancellation adds a second hidden GameObject with its own per-frame Update poll (LifecycleCancellation.cs:229-238, 277-280) and AndroidAppPauseListener a third (AndroidAppPauseListener.cs:12-19). The asmdef (TurboHTTP.Unity.asmdef) has no defineConstraints and none of the hooks checks whether the feature is used.

**Failure scenario.** A project that only wants UseAdaptiveNetworking (or only PathSafety downloads, or nothing from TurboHTTP.Unity at all but links it, see unity-design-01) gets a dispatcher GameObject in the DontDestroyOnLoad scene, a system appended to its PlayerLoop, a drain call with two lock acquisitions and one allocation every frame (unity-design-10), a main-thread file-system sweep before the first scene, and static roots for the texture scheduler, temp-file manager and decoder registry. The dispatcher (1,033 + 722 lines), the temp-file manager and the scheduler are therefore unstrippable in any build that links the assembly.

## Suggested fix
Create the dispatcher lazily on first main-thread use (keep only a cheap BeforeSceneLoad hook that records the main thread id), run the temp-file sweep lazily from the first audio call on a worker thread, and make the reset hooks no-ops that do not instantiate singletons. Longer term split the assembly: TurboHTTP.Unity (dispatcher, lifecycle, coroutines), TurboHTTP.Unity.Assets (texture/audio/decoders/temp files), TurboHTTP.Unity.Mobile.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The dispatcher is created lazily on first main-thread use; the BeforeSceneLoad hook only records the main thread id
- [ ] The temp-file sweep runs lazily on first audio use on a worker thread, and SubsystemRegistration reset hooks do not instantiate singletons
- [ ] A project that uses no TurboHTTP.Unity feature has no dispatcher GameObject, no PlayerLoop system and no lowMemory subscription at startup
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (assert no dispatcher instance or PlayerLoop system exists after startup until first use)

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-design-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced: MainThreadDispatcher.BootstrapBeforeSceneLoad (MainThreadDispatcher.cs:242-250) always calls EnsureInstanceReady, which creates the DontDestroyOnLoad GameObject (:697-699); Awake subscribes Application.lowMemory and installs the PlayerLoop system (:280-283). AudioClipHandler.RuntimeInitialize (AudioClipHandler.cs:123-127) -> UnityTempFileManager.EnsureStartupSweep, a synchronous Directory.GetFiles(AllDirectories)+delete on the main thread when the temp root exists (UnityTempFileManager.cs:166-191). TextureDecodeScheduler.ResetStaticState touches Shared and subscribes lowMemory (TextureDecodeScheduler.cs:97-121). No feature-use check and no defineConstraints in TurboHTTP.Unity.asmdef. Two details overstated: the LifecycleCancellation driver GameObject is created lazily on the first Bind with a non-null owner (LifecycleCancellation.cs:138-143, 229-238), and AndroidAppPauseListener is compiled only under UNITY_ANDROID && !UNITY_EDITOR && TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING (AndroidAppPauseListener.cs:1). The remaining SubsystemRegistration hooks are cheap static resets. #182 (oversized files) does not track this.

title: [Unity] MainThreadDispatcher stops draining when the PlayerLoop is replaced after install because the Update fallback stays disabled
body:
## Summary
TryInstallPlayerLoop sets _playerLoopInstalled and appends a marker system, and Update() dispatches only when that flag is 0. Nothing re-checks that the marker is still present. If another package calls PlayerLoop.SetPlayerLoop with a loop built from the default one, the marker disappears while the flag stays 1, so queued work is never drained.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/MainThreadDispatcher.cs:290`

## Problem
TryInstallPlayerLoop sets _playerLoopInstalled to 1 and appends a PlayerLoopDispatchMarker system to the current loop (826-849). Update() dispatches only when _playerLoopInstalled == 0 (287-294). Nothing re-checks that the marker is still present: ContainsPlayerLoopType is called only at install and uninstall (834, 864). Code elsewhere that builds its loop from PlayerLoop.GetDefaultPlayerLoop() and calls SetPlayerLoop removes the marker.

**Failure scenario.** Dispatcher Awake at BeforeSceneLoad installs the hook; a later bootstrap calls PlayerLoop.SetPlayerLoop with a loop built from the default one -> marker gone, flag still 1 -> every ExecuteAsync from a worker thread (texture and audio finalization, WebSocket events, lifecycle driver creation) stays queued; calls without a token never complete, and after 512 items new work is rejected. Confirm with a PlayMode test that resets the loop and dispatches from Task.Run.

## Suggested fix
Make the MonoBehaviour a real fallback: dispatch from Update or LateUpdate when _lastDispatchFrame is more than one frame behind Time.frameCount (the per-frame guard already prevents double dispatch), and reinstall the hook when the marker is missing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The dispatcher drains the queue from Update/LateUpdate when the PlayerLoop hook has not run for more than one frame, and reinstalls the hook when the marker is missing
- [ ] After PlayerLoop.SetPlayerLoop replaces the loop, work dispatched from Task.Run completes
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (PlayMode test that resets the player loop and dispatches from a worker thread)

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-runtime-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: platform-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. TryInstallPlayerLoop sets _playerLoopInstalled=1 and appends the marker system (Runtime/Unity/MainThreadDispatcher.cs:826-849); Update() dispatches only when the flag is 0 (287-294); ContainsPlayerLoopType is called only at install (834) and uninstall (864); the flag is cleared only in ResetStaticState (228) or on an install exception (852). No code re-checks the marker and no test covers a replaced loop (rg PlayerLoop Tests/ = no hits). If any code calls PlayerLoop.SetPlayerLoop with a loop not derived from the current one after Awake, PlayerLoopDispatch is gone, the fallback stays disabled and queued work is never drained (default UserQueueCapacity 512, MainThreadWorkQueue.cs:61). The trigger is third-party or app code (e.g. a loop built from GetDefaultPlayerLoop), not default behaviour, so medium at most; the outcome once triggered is deterministic.

title: [Unity] Destroying the MainThreadDispatcher GameObject leaves the dispatcher rejecting all work for the rest of the process
body:
## Summary
OnDestroy calls BeginShutdown(Disposing), which sets a terminal state, and only ResetStaticState (SubsystemRegistration) leaves it. Execute and ExecuteAsync check availability before the main-thread inline path, so even calls on the main thread throw. If a game clears its DontDestroyOnLoad objects, GetTextureAsync, AsTexture2D, AsSprite, audio finalization and LifecycleCancellation driver creation throw InvalidOperationException, and UnityWebSocketBridge logs an exception per incoming message.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/MainThreadDispatcher.cs:306`

## Problem
OnDestroy calls BeginShutdown(..., Disposing) (306-316, 782-799), which sets the terminal state, nulls _instance and makes the queue reject. EnsureInstanceReady calls RejectIfUnavailable before it would create a new instance (684), and Execute, ExecuteAsync and ExecuteControlAsync call RejectIfUnavailable before their IsMainThread inline paths (350, 382, 425, 455, 479). Only ResetStaticState (SubsystemRegistration, 218-240) leaves the terminal state; the reliability test recovers only by calling that internal method (UnityReliabilitySuiteTests.cs:125-131). No test destroys the dispatcher object while the player keeps running.

**Failure scenario.** A game clears its DontDestroyOnLoad objects for a soft restart (or any code destroys '[TurboHTTP MainThreadDispatcher]') -> for the rest of the process GetTextureAsync, AsTexture2D, AsSprite, AsAudioClipAsync and LifecycleCancellation driver creation throw InvalidOperationException 'MainThreadDispatcher is disposing', and UnityWebSocketBridge logs one exception per incoming message (DispatchCore catch -> OnUserLaneFailed -> Debug.LogException, UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:325-333, 549-552). In the Editor the state also stays Reloading in edit mode after a play session until the next reload.

## Suggested fix
Separate application quit and domain reload (terminal) from an unexpected destroy: on a non-quit OnDestroy fail the queued work but return to Uninitialized so the next main-thread access recreates the instance, and let inline execution on the main thread run regardless of lifecycle state.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A non-quit OnDestroy of the dispatcher fails queued work and returns to Uninitialized so the next main-thread access recreates the instance
- [ ] Inline execution on the main thread works regardless of lifecycle state; only application quit and domain reload are terminal
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (destroy the dispatcher object while running, assert the next ExecuteAsync succeeds)

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-runtime-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: resource-management.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. OnDestroy -> BeginShutdown(Disposing) (MainThreadDispatcher.cs:306-316) sets the terminal state, RejectNewWork and _instance=null (782-799). The only exit from Disposing/Reloading is ResetStaticState (218-240, SubsystemRegistration). EnsureInstanceReady calls RejectIfUnavailable before creating a new host (684); Execute/ExecuteAsync/ExecuteControlAsync call RejectIfUnavailable before the IsMainThread inline path (350, 382, 425, 455, 479), and EnsureInitializedIfMainThread returns early because state != Uninitialized (712). So destroying the DontDestroyOnLoad host (not hidden: no hideFlags at 697) at runtime makes AsTexture2D/GetTextureAsync/AsSprite/audio finalization throw InvalidOperationException for the rest of the process. The only recovery test calls the internal ResetStaticState (Tests/Runtime/Unity/UnityReliabilitySuiteTests.cs:125-131). No guard found. Needs an explicit destroy of the host object, so medium.

title: [Unity] MainThreadDispatcher.Enqueue runs inline on the main thread and Execute*Async report failure through three different channels
body:
## Summary
Enqueue wraps ExecuteAsync, which executes inline on the main thread by default, so fire-and-forget deferral is synchronous re-entrancy there. ExecuteAsync throws synchronously for a null action and for uninitialized or disposing states, returns Task.FromException for inline failures and faults the task for queue rejection. Callers that defer work from the main thread get immediate execution, and a worker calling Enqueue during quit gets an exception on its own thread.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/MainThreadDispatcher.cs:321`

## Problem
Enqueue wraps ExecuteAsync (321-336), which executes inline when called on the main thread with the default AllowInlineExecutionOnMainThread = true (352-364), so 'Enqueues fire-and-forget work' is synchronous re-entrancy there. ExecuteAsync throws synchronously for a null action, an uninitialized dispatcher called from a worker (723-725) and a disposing/reloading dispatcher (807), returns Task.FromException for an inline action failure (360-363), and faults the task for queue rejection. Internal callers already defend against the synchronous throw (UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:325-333, LifecycleCancellation.cs:215-226).

**Failure scenario.** Code that calls MainThreadDispatcher.Enqueue from the main thread to defer work until after the current callback (for example to avoid modifying a collection it is iterating) has the action run immediately. A worker that calls the fire-and-forget Enqueue during application quit gets InvalidOperationException thrown on its own thread.

## Suggested fix
Make Enqueue always queue (never inline) and never throw for lifecycle states; return faulted tasks from the Execute*Async methods for every non-argument failure.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Enqueue always queues and never runs the action inline
- [ ] Execute*Async methods throw synchronously only for argument errors and return faulted tasks for every other failure, including lifecycle states
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (Enqueue from the main thread does not run before it returns; Enqueue during shutdown does not throw)
