title: [Unity] GetTextureAsync copies the whole encoded body (twice with MaxPixels) and holds the pooled response through the decode queue
body:
## Summary
ValidatePixelGuardFromHeader flattens the body with ToArray only to read the image header, then PrepareDecodeInput flattens it again for the DecodeInput. Buffered bodies are pooled 16 KB segments, so the copy is the normal case, and the response stays alive across the queue wait. With many concurrent images this holds roughly three times the encoded size in managed memory before any texture exists.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/Texture2DHandler.cs:499`

## Problem
PrepareDecodeInput (378-397) calls ValidatePixelGuardFromHeader, which runs GetDecodeBytes(imageBytes), i.e. body.ToArray(), only to read the PNG or JPEG header (494-501, 556-562), then calls GetDecodeBytes(response.Body) again for the DecodeInput (396). TryGetExactArray (564-578) avoids the copy only for a single exactly-sized array; buffered bodies are 16 KB pooled segments or a rented array (architecture.md 'Shared infrastructure', UHttpResponse.cs:104-115), so the copy is the normal case. GetTextureAsync holds 'using var response' across ScheduleAsync (131-169), so the pooled body and the private copy both live through the queue wait (up to MaxQueuedDecodes = 128 entries) and the decode.

**Failure scenario.** 100 concurrent 1 MB thumbnails with MaxPixels set -> 100 MB of throwaway large-object arrays for the header check, plus 100 MB of copies and 100 MB of pooled segments retained while items wait for one of 2 decode slots: about three times the encoded size in managed memory before any texture exists.

## Suggested fix
Read the dimensions from the sequence without flattening (first segment for PNG, a bounded scan for JPEG), make one copy, capture content type and path, and dispose the response before queuing the decode.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The image header is read from the body sequence without flattening it.
- [ ] At most one copy of the encoded body is made per GetTextureAsync call, and the response is disposed before the decode is queued.
- [ ] Target: with MaxPixels set, 100 concurrent 1 MB images allocate at most 100 MB of temporary arrays (one copy each), measured with a test allocation counter.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix by counting body flattenings.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-runtime-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. ValidatePixelGuardFromHeader calls GetDecodeBytes(imageBytes) = body.ToArray() just to read the header when MaxPixels is set (Texture2DHandler.cs:494-501, 556-562), then PrepareDecodeInput calls GetDecodeBytes(response.Body) again (396). TryGetExactArray (564-578) only avoids the copy for one exactly-sized array; buffered responses are SegmentedBuffer sequences of 16 KB segments (Runtime/Core/Pipeline/ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:147-222), so any image over 16 KB is copied. GetTextureAsync keeps 'using var response' alive across ScheduleAsync (131-169) and DecodeScheduledAsync only needs Content-Type and the path from it (295-296), so pooled segments plus the private copy live through the queue wait (MaxQueuedDecodes 128, 2 workers). One copy is unavoidable (LoadImage takes byte[]); the second copy and the retained pooled body are waste, and the security option (MaxPixels) is what doubles the allocation. Large arrays on Unity's non-compacting GC make this more than cosmetic on mobile.

Related: #120, [[R11-unity-design-34]], [[R11-unity-protocol-07]].

title: [Unity] Texture2DHandler MaxPixels pre-decode guard fails open on unparseable headers and its JPEG scanner is defeated by fill bytes
body:
## Summary
ValidatePixelGuardFromHeader returns without error when TryReadImageDimensions fails, and TryReadJpegDimensions treats every 0xFF as a marker with a two-byte length. A fill byte or a length-less marker such as TEM or RSTn makes it read a bogus length and give up, so the limit is only enforced after LoadImage has already allocated the image. A hostile server can use this to bypass a configured MaxPixels. The verifier rated this plausible because the outcome depends on Unity accepting the fill bytes.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/Texture2DHandler.cs:500`

## Problem
ValidatePixelGuardFromHeader returns without error when TryReadImageDimensions fails (lines 499-501). TryReadJpegDimensions (610-655) assumes every 0xFF is followed by a marker with a two-byte length: a fill byte (FF FF before a marker, legal padding) or a parameterless marker such as TEM (FF 01) or RSTn makes it read the following marker bytes as a length (line 634), e.g. FF D8 FF FF C0 ... yields segmentLength 0xC000 and the loop breaks at 635-636 returning false. Only PNG and JPEG are recognised at all (580-592). The remaining check runs after texture.LoadImage returned (530-538), i.e. after the full allocation and decode. The only test uses a well-formed PNG (Tests/Runtime/Unity/TexturePipelineV2Tests.cs:30-40).

**Failure scenario.** An application sets MaxPixels = 4_000_000. A server returns a JPEG whose SOF0 is preceded by one 0xFF fill byte and declares 16000x16000. The pre-check returns 'unknown' and lets it through; LoadImage decodes 256M pixels before the post-check throws. The limit that was configured to prevent the allocation did not prevent it.

## Suggested fix
When MaxPixels is set, fail closed: reject payloads whose dimensions cannot be established, and parse JPEG markers per ITU T.81 (skip fill bytes, treat SOI/TEM/RSTn as length-less). Keep the post-decode check as a second line only.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When MaxPixels is set, a payload whose dimensions cannot be established is rejected before LoadImage.
- [ ] The JPEG scanner skips fill bytes and treats SOI, TEM and RSTn as length-less markers per ITU T.81.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Unity/TexturePipelineV2Tests.cs fails before the fix: a JPEG with a fill byte before SOF0 declaring a large size is rejected without calling LoadImage.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-protocol-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: security.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Parser trace holds. ValidatePixelGuardFromHeader returns silently when TryReadImageDimensions fails (Texture2DHandler.cs:499-501). In TryReadJpegDimensions (610-655) the bytes FF D8 FF FF C0 00 11 ... give marker = 0xFF at index 2 and segmentLength = 0xC000 (line 634); for a payload under ~49 KB the loop breaks at 635-636 and returns false; larger payloads jump into entropy data and end at EOI/SOS, also false. Only PNG and JPEG are recognised (580-592). The remaining check is after LoadImage returned (530-538). Only test is a well-formed PNG (TexturePipelineV2Tests.cs:30-40). Outcome depends on Unity's JPEG decoder accepting fill bytes (legal per ITU T.81 B.1.1.2, accepted by libjpeg) and on its allocation behaviour, not provable here. Applies only when MaxPixels is configured.

Related: [[R11-unity-protocol-06]], [[R11-unity-runtime-09]].

title: [Unity] TextureOptions has no default bound on decoded pixels, although the docs say it protects against hostile images
body:
## Summary
MaxBodyBytes, MaxSourceBytes and MaxPixels all default to null, so with default options untrusted bytes go straight to Texture2D.LoadImage on the main thread with MipMaps enabled. Documentation~/Modules/Unity.md states that TextureOptions bounds the work so a hostile image cannot exhaust memory. Source bytes are bounded by the 100 MB buffered body limit, but decoded size is not, so a small PNG declaring a very large image can exhaust memory on mobile.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/Texture2DHandler.cs:522`

## Problem
TextureOptions.MaxBodyBytes, MaxSourceBytes and MaxPixels are nullable and default to null (lines 39, 45, 50). ValidateBodyLength returns when no limit is set (463-467) and ValidatePixelGuardFromHeader returns when MaxPixels is null (494-497), so with default options DecodeTexture hands the untrusted bytes straight to Texture2D.LoadImage on the main thread (511-524) with MipMaps = true. Documentation~/Modules/Unity.md:30 states: 'TextureOptions bounds the work (MaxBodyBytes, MaxPixels, concurrent decodes) so a hostile image cannot exhaust memory.' Only the scheduler concurrency has a default.

**Failure scenario.** A game loads avatar URLs supplied by other players with client.GetTextureAsync(url). An attacker serves a few-hundred-kilobyte PNG declaring 16384x16384 (or the device's max texture size) of a single colour: LoadImage allocates width*height*4 bytes plus the mip chain (about 1.4 GB at 16384, about 350 MB at 8192) and stalls the main thread while inflating, which kills the app on mobile.

## Suggested fix
Ship finite defaults (for example MaxPixels of 4096x4096 or SystemInfo.maxTextureSize squared capped, and a MaxSourceBytes) and make 'no limit' the explicit opt-out; reject before LoadImage when the header dimensions exceed the bound.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] TextureOptions ships finite defaults for MaxPixels and MaxSourceBytes, and removing the limit is an explicit opt-out.
- [ ] Images whose header dimensions exceed the bound are rejected before LoadImage.
- [ ] Documentation~/Modules/Unity.md matches the defaults.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix: a PNG header declaring 16384x16384 is rejected with default options.

## Context

title: [Unity] TextureDecodeScheduler runs decode delegates inside its _gate lock, nesting a stack level per queued image
body:
## Summary
ScheduleAsync and Configure call PumpWorkers_NoLock while holding the scheduler lock, and that method invokes RunDecodeAsync synchronously. The synchronous prefix of the decode, including decoder registry resolution, custom IImageDecoder code and an inline Texture2D.LoadImage on the main thread, therefore runs under the lock. Worker threads calling ScheduleAsync or GetMetrics block for the whole decode, and a backlog is drained by recursion instead of the concurrency limit.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/TextureDecodeScheduler.cs:219`

## Problem
ScheduleAsync and Configure call PumpWorkers_NoLock inside lock (_gate) (144-148, 167-189); it invokes RunDecodeAsync synchronously (215-220), whose prefix up to the first incomplete await runs item.DecodeAsync (245), i.e. Texture2DHandler.DecodeScheduledAsync: DecoderRegistry resolution, Debug.LogWarning, the synchronous part of a custom IImageDecoder.DecodeAsync (Texture2DHandler.cs:298-315) and, when the caller is on the main thread, an inline MainThreadDispatcher.ExecuteAsync that performs Texture2D.LoadImage (263-266). The finally block re-enters the lock and pumps the next item recursively (256-266).

**Failure scenario.** GetTextureAsync continues synchronously on the main thread (cache hit or mock transport): the whole LoadImage runs inside the scheduler lock, worker threads calling ScheduleAsync or GetMetrics block for the decode, and a backlog is drained by nested recursion (one stack level per queued image) rather than by the concurrency limit.

## Suggested fix
Collect the items to start under the lock and invoke RunDecodeAsync after releasing it (or start each with Task.Run), so no user or Unity code runs under _gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No decoder, dispatcher or Unity API code runs while TextureDecodeScheduler._gate is held; items to start are collected under the lock and started after it is released.
- [ ] Draining a backlog of N queued images does not grow the stack by one level per image.
- [ ] The MaxConcurrent limit is still honoured and metrics stay consistent.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (a synchronously completing decode delegate does not hold the lock and does not recurse).

title: [Unity] DownloadToPersistentDataAsync and DownloadToTempCacheAsync read Application paths on the calling thread and throw off the main thread
body:
## Summary
The four download helpers in UnityExtensions evaluate Application.persistentDataPath or Application.temporaryCachePath as an argument before any await. Those properties are main-thread only, so a call from Task.Run or after ConfigureAwait(false) throws UnityException synchronously from a Task-returning API in the Editor and development players. UnityTempFileManager already caches its root at BeforeSceneLoad for this reason, but the helpers do not.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/UnityExtensions.cs:28`

## Problem
DownloadToPersistentDataAsync and DownloadToTempCacheAsync evaluate Application.persistentDataPath or Application.temporaryCachePath as an argument before any await (28, 48, 67, 87). These properties are main-thread only (platform.md 'Unity main thread'); UnityTempFileManager caches its root at BeforeSceneLoad for exactly this reason (UnityTempFileManager.cs:412-418). The helpers neither cache nor dispatch.

**Failure scenario.** 'await client.DownloadToPersistentDataAsync(url, path)' from Task.Run, or after an await with ConfigureAwait(false), in the Editor or a development player -> UnityException 'get_persistentDataPath can only be called from the main thread' is thrown synchronously from an API that returns Task. In release players the check is compiled out and the call reaches native code off-thread.

## Suggested fix
Cache both roots on the main thread at startup (the RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod pattern of UnityTempFileManager.CacheRootPath) and use the cached values.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both roots are cached on the main thread at startup (as UnityTempFileManager.CacheRootPath does) and the helpers use the cached values.
- [ ] Calling the helpers from a thread-pool thread does not throw UnityException; errors surface through the returned Task.
- [ ] The helpers behave sensibly when called before the cache is initialised (documented fallback or clear exception).
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (helpers invoked from a non-main thread with an injected path provider).

## Context

Verifier note: Code is as described: all four helpers evaluate Application.persistentDataPath / temporaryCachePath as an argument on the calling thread before any await (UnityExtensions.cs:28, 48, 67, 87); nothing caches or dispatches. The project treats these as main-thread only (Development~/docs/agents/platform.md:56) and UnityTempFileManager caches its root at BeforeSceneLoad for that reason (UnityTempFileManager.cs:412-418). Called from Task.Run or after ConfigureAwait(false), the Editor/development player throws UnityException synchronously from a Task-returning API. No guard or doc restriction found (Documentation~/Modules/Unity.md:49-50 shows plain awaits). title: [Unity] UnityExtensions.DownloadTo*Async buffers the whole body (100 MB cap) instead of reusing the streaming FileDownloader
body:
## Summary
DownloadToUnityPathAsync uses SendBufferedAsync and then PathSafety.WriteAtomicAsync, so the entire body is held in memory and is capped by MaxBufferedResponseBodySize (100 MB). FileDownloader in the Files module already streams to a .part file with resume, validators and incremental SHA-256, and reports ChecksumMismatchException. The Unity docs present both as equivalent for large asset packs, so a 300 MB pack fails at 100 MB or occupies hundreds of MB of managed memory on a phone, and checksum errors surface as a different exception type.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/UnityExtensions.cs:127`

## Problem
DownloadToUnityPathAsync calls client.Get(url).SendBufferedAsync (127) and hands the buffered body to PathSafety.WriteAtomicAsync (131-136); multi-segment bodies are copied once more by ToBodyMemory (146-155). Buffered responses are capped by UHttpClientOptions.MaxBufferedResponseBodySize, default 100 MB (Runtime/Core/UHttpClientOptions.cs:107-123). Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs streams to destinationPath + '.part' with resume, validators and incremental SHA-256 and throws ChecksumMismatchException (86-141, 591-593, 707-735). PathSafety has its own root containment (69-95), its own temp naming ('.tmp-<guid>', 307-313), validates the checksum only after the temp file is written (142-143) and reports a mismatch as InvalidOperationException (211-212). Documentation~/Modules/Unity.md recommends DownloadToPersistentDataAsync for 'pack.zip' and for AssetBundles 'or FileDownloader' as equivalents. The duplication exists because Unity may reference only Core.

**Failure scenario.** An app follows the docs and downloads a 300 MB asset pack with DownloadToPersistentDataAsync: the request fails at the 100 MB buffered-body limit after downloading 100 MB; with the limit raised, 300 MB (twice that for a multi-segment body) sits in managed memory on a phone before the first byte reaches disk, there is no resume, and a checksum mismatch surfaces as a different exception type than the Files module uses.

## Suggested fix
Keep only path resolution (ResolvePathWithinRoot against persistentDataPath/temporaryCachePath) in TurboHTTP.Unity and route the transfer through one streaming implementation: either a streaming-to-file primitive in Core that both modules use, or a documented Unity-to-Files reference exception. Until then document the buffering and the size limit on the Unity helpers and make PathSafety internal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unity download helpers stream to disk through one shared streaming implementation (or a documented Unity-to-Files reference), with no full-body buffering.
- [ ] A download larger than MaxBufferedResponseBodySize completes without raising that limit.
- [ ] Checksum mismatch raises the same exception type as FileDownloader, and PathSafety is internal or reduced to path resolution.
- [ ] Documentation~/Modules/Unity.md describes size behaviour and resume support accurately.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (large body streamed, memory bounded; checksum mismatch type).

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-design-15` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. DownloadToUnityPathAsync buffers the whole body with client.Get(url).SendBufferedAsync (Runtime/Unity/UnityExtensions.cs:127) and passes it to PathSafety.WriteAtomicAsync (131-136); ToBodyMemory copies a multi-segment body again with body.ToArray() (146-155). Buffered bodies are capped at 100 MB by default and a larger body fails the request (Runtime/Core/UHttpClientOptions.cs:107-123). PathSafety writes the temp file first and validates the SHA-256 afterwards (PathSafety.cs:142-143), throws InvalidOperationException on mismatch (211-212), uses '.tmp-<guid>' naming (307-313) and is a public static class (36). Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs streams to '.part' with resume and ChecksumMismatchException (34, 55, 86-124). Documentation~/Modules/Unity.md:49-57 shows DownloadToPersistentDataAsync for 'pack.zip' and for AssetBundles '(or FileDownloader)' with no word about buffering or the size cap; only QuickStart.md:167 warns about buffered responses in general. TurboHTTP.Unity.asmdef references only TurboHTTP.Core, but that does not force buffering: Core already has SendStreamingAsync, so the helper could stream to the temp file without a Files reference. No guard, test or issue refutes it; #122 (AssetBundle handler) does not cover it.

title: [Unity] Temp-file manager, PathSafety and platform bridges are public without XML docs, and audio temp config has two diverging entry points
body:
## Summary
UnityTempFileManager is public although it is hard-wired to audio and used only by AudioClipHandler, and AudioClipHandler.Configure and UnityTempFileManager.Shared.Configure both change the same options, so the second leaves AudioClipHandler.GetOptions() stale. PathSafety, TextureDecodeScheduler, DecoderRegistry, LifecycleCancellation.Bind and the iOS/Android background bridges are public too, and over 200 public members of public types in the slice have no XML summary. Plumbing that cannot change without a breaking release would be frozen at GA, and customers get no IntelliSense for options such as BackgroundNetworkingPolicy.QueueOnAppPause.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/UnityTempFileManager.cs:84`

## Problem
UnityTempFileManager is public with Shared, Configure, TryReservePath, WriteBytesAsync and ReleaseAndScheduleDelete (84-283) although it is hard-wired to audio (folder 'audio', prefix 'turbohttp-audio-', 86-88) and only used by AudioClipHandler; AudioClipHandler.Configure overwrites its options (AudioClipHandler.cs:158-165) while a direct UnityTempFileManager.Shared.Configure leaves AudioClipHandler.GetOptions() reporting stale values. PathSafety, TextureDecodeScheduler, DecoderRegistry, LifecycleCancellation.Bind, MainThreadDispatcherWorkKind, IosBackgroundTaskBridge and AndroidBackgroundWorkBridge are public as well. A scan of the slice finds well over 200 public members of public types without an XML summary, for example every member of MainThreadDispatcherSettings/Metrics (MainThreadWorkQueue.cs:99-194), UnityWebSocketBridge's IWebSocketClient surface and events (UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:35-131), UnityWebSocketClient's Connect/Send/IsConnected (UnityWebSocketClient.cs:98-326), BackgroundNetworkingInterceptor and BackgroundNetworkingPolicy (no docs at all), NetworkQuality.cs, the WebSocket UniTask extensions and UnityWebSocketExtensions. CLAUDE.md requires XML docs on public API and prefers internal.

**Failure scenario.** The public surface that will be frozen at GA includes plumbing that cannot be changed without a breaking release (for example the temp-file manager's path reservation API), and customers get no IntelliSense for options such as BackgroundNetworkingPolicy.QueueOnAppPause.

## Suggested fix
Before the API freeze make UnityTempFileManager, PathSafety, TextureDecodeScheduler internals and the platform bridges internal (expose only options/metrics), keep a single configuration entry point for audio, and add the missing XML docs to what stays public.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Plumbing types (UnityTempFileManager, PathSafety, scheduler internals, platform bridges) are internal; only options and metrics types stay public.
- [ ] Audio temp-file configuration has a single public entry point and GetOptions() always reflects it.
- [ ] Every remaining public member of the Unity module has an XML summary.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (configuration through the single entry point is reflected by GetOptions()).

title: [Unity] UnityTempFileManager startup sweep deletes turbohttp-audio-* files in use by another running instance of the same app
body:
## Summary
EnsureStartupSweep deletes every turbohttp-audio-* file under a root derived only from Application.temporaryCachePath, which is shared per company and product rather than per process. Nothing marks a file as owned by a live process, so a second desktop instance, or the Editor and a standalone build of the same project, unlinks files the first instance is still loading or streaming.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/UnityTempFileManager.cs:177`

## Problem
EnsureStartupSweep enumerates Directory.GetFiles(root, "turbohttp-audio-*", AllDirectories) and deletes each (lines 166-191); it runs at BeforeSceneLoad (AudioClipHandler.cs:123-127) and on first use. The root is derived only from Application.temporaryCachePath (431-434), which is per company/product, not per process, so two desktop instances, or the Editor and a standalone build of the same project, share it. Nothing marks a file as owned by a live process.

**Failure scenario.** Instance A is playing a streamed clip (file kept until the clip is destroyed) or sits between WriteBytesAsync and the UnityWebRequest load; instance B starts and its sweep unlinks A's files: A's load fails with 'Failed to decode audio clip from temp file', or on platforms where the delete succeeds on an open file the stream loses its backing file.

## Suggested fix
Put files under a per-process subdirectory (process id plus start time or a session GUID with a lock file) and sweep only directories whose owner is gone.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Temp files live under a per-process (or per-session) subdirectory, and the sweep deletes only directories whose owner process is gone.
- [ ] A second instance starting does not delete files belonging to a live instance.
- [ ] Stale files of crashed instances are still removed.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (sweep with a live-owner directory and a dead-owner directory).

title: [Unity] AudioClipHandler.Configure and UnityTempFileManager.Configure dispose semaphores that in-flight loads still hold
body:
## Summary
Configure replaces and disposes _decodeLimiter and _ioLimiter while operations may be holding or waiting on the old instance. Releasing a disposed SemaphoreSlim throws ObjectDisposedException and waiters never complete, and WriteBytesAsync reads the _ioLimiter field twice so it can release a different semaphore than it acquired (SemaphoreFullException). Reconfiguring while clips load makes loads fail after the clip was created, hang, or fail after the file was written.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/UnityTempFileManager.cs:229`

## Problem
AudioClipHandler.Configure replaces _decodeLimiter and disposes the old one when MaxConcurrentDecodes changes (AudioClipHandler.cs:148-155); AsAudioClipAsync captured the old instance (190) and calls limiter.Release() in finally (216-219). SemaphoreSlim.Release throws ObjectDisposedException after Dispose and pending WaitAsync callers are never completed. UnityTempFileManager.Configure does the same with _ioLimiter (UnityTempFileManager.cs:157-162), and WriteBytesAsync reads the field twice: await _ioLimiter.WaitAsync (229) and _ioLimiter.Release() (263); ProcessDeleteQueueAsync likewise (319, 334). ResetStaticState repeats both swaps (AudioClipHandler.cs:115-119, UnityTempFileManager.cs:125-129). AudioPipelineV2Tests only reconfigures while idle.

**Failure scenario.** A settings screen calls AudioClipHandler.Configure(new AudioClipPipelineOptions { MaxConcurrentDecodes = 4, TempMaxConcurrentIo = 4 }) while clips are loading. A load that already decoded its AudioClip hits limiter.Release() on the disposed semaphore: ObjectDisposedException replaces the result and the created clip is never destroyed or returned. Loads waiting in WaitAsync on the old limiter hang forever. A WriteBytesAsync that waited on the old I/O limiter releases the new, full one: SemaphoreFullException escapes the finally and the load fails after the file was written.

## Suggested fix
Never dispose a limiter that may be held: capture the instance in a local for wait and release, let replaced semaphores be collected, or implement resizing by adjusting permits on one long-lived semaphore.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No limiter is disposed while it may be held; each operation captures the instance used for wait and release.
- [ ] Reconfiguring MaxConcurrentDecodes or TempMaxConcurrentIo during in-flight loads neither throws ObjectDisposedException or SemaphoreFullException nor leaves waiters hanging.
- [ ] Created AudioClips are returned or destroyed on every path, including when Configure races the load.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (Configure called while loads hold and wait on the limiter).

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-design-11` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: AudioClipHandler.Configure swaps and disposes _decodeLimiter when MaxConcurrentDecodes changes (AudioClipHandler.cs:148-155); AsAudioClipAsync captured the old instance (:190) and calls limiter.Release() in finally (:216-219), which throws ObjectDisposedException on a disposed SemaphoreSlim, and waiters parked in WaitAsync (:192) on the disposed instance are never released unless their token fires. UnityTempFileManager.Configure does the same with _ioLimiter (UnityTempFileManager.cs:157-162); WriteBytesAsync reads the field at wait (:229) and again at release (:263), ProcessDeleteQueueAsync likewise (:319, :334), so after a swap the release goes to the new, full semaphore (SemaphoreFullException) and the old permit is never returned. ResetStaticState repeats both swaps (AudioClipHandler.cs:115-119, UnityTempFileManager.cs:125-129). No lock or generation check covers in-flight holders; AudioPipelineV2Tests reconfigures only while idle (:16, :36). Needs Configure with a changed limit while loads are in flight, an edge case.

Also reported as `unity-runtime-12`, `unity-runtime-13` (merged into this issue).

title: [Mobile] Audio temp files go to Application.temporaryCachePath, the shared external cache on Android 10 and earlier
body:
## Summary
UnityTempFileManager writes downloaded audio under Application.temporaryCachePath, which Unity maps to the app's external cache directory on Android when external storage is available. On API 29 and lower an app holding storage permissions can read or replace files there, and the file is reopened by file:// URI with no integrity check. A co-installed app could substitute audio bytes before they reach the native decoder or read private audio.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/UnityTempFileManager.cs:433`

## Problem
ReadRootPath returns Path.Combine(Application.temporaryCachePath, "TurboHTTP", "audio") (lines 431-434). DecodeViaUnityTempPathAsync writes the downloaded body there (AudioClipHandler.cs:346-348), closes it, and LoadAudioClipCoroutine reopens it by file:// URI through UnityWebRequestMultimedia (AudioClipHandler.cs:387, 418); streamed clips keep reading the file for the clip's lifetime (StreamedAudioTempFiles.cs). On Android Unity maps temporaryCachePath to the app's external cache dir (/storage/emulated/0/Android/data/<package>/cache) when external storage is available; before scoped storage (API 29 and lower, Unity 2021.3 minimum is API 22) apps holding the storage permissions can read and write it. The file is opened with FileMode.Create and no later integrity check (UnityTempFileManager.cs:238).

**Failure scenario.** On an Android 9 device a second app with WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE watches the cache directory, and replaces turbohttp-audio-<guid>.ogg between WriteBytesAsync and the UnityWebRequest load (or while a streamed clip plays): bytes that arrived over TLS are substituted before they reach Unity's native audio decoder, and licensed or private audio is readable by any app with READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE. Needs device validation of the path and Android version.

## Suggested fix
Resolve an app-internal directory on Android (Context.getCacheDir() through the existing JNI thread) for the temp root, or avoid the file round trip for non-streamed clips; mark needs-device-validation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On Android the temp root is an app-internal directory (Context.getCacheDir() via the existing JNI thread), or non-streamed clips avoid the file round trip.
- [ ] The chosen path and Android API level behaviour are documented.
- [ ] The change is validated on an Android device or emulator at API 29 or lower and recorded.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it (root resolution uses an injected platform path provider).

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-protocol-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: security.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Code as described: ReadRootPath = Path.Combine(Application.temporaryCachePath, "TurboHTTP", "audio") (UnityTempFileManager.cs:431-434); WriteBytesAsync uses FileMode.Create with no later integrity check (238); the file is reopened by file:// URI (AudioClipHandler.cs:387, 418). No internal-cache resolution or documentation of the trade-off found. Whether temporaryCachePath maps to the external app cache dir and whether another app can read/replace it depends on Unity's Android path choice and API level (pre scoped storage only): needs-device-validation. Downgraded to low: requires a co-installed malicious app with storage permission on Android 10 or earlier, and the content is audio, not credentials.

Related: [[R11-unity-protocol-19]].

title: [Packaging] Runtime/Unity/link.xml preserves ten decoder types by reflection rules nothing needs, rooting TurboHTTP.Unity in every build
body:
## Summary
Runtime/Unity/link.xml preserves all ten decoder types with preserve="all", including the three stubs that always throw (#158). The decoders are created with static new expressions and used through interfaces, so no reflection path needs the rules. Because TurboHTTP.Unity.dll is always in the linker input, the merged link.xml roots the assembly and about 1.2k lines of decoder code and its startup hooks in every stripped player, including HTTP-only projects.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/link.xml:2`

## Problem
link.xml:3-12 lists IImageDecoder, IAudioDecoder, DecodedImage, DecodedAudio, DecoderRegistry, StbImageSharpDecoder, WavPcmDecoder, AiffPcmDecoder, NVorbisDecoder, NLayerMp3Decoder with preserve="all". Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:146-150 merges every Runtime/**/link.xml whose owning DLL is in the linker input directory, and TurboHTTP.Unity.dll always is (asmdef has no platform or define constraint, Runtime/Unity/TurboHTTP.Unity.asmdef:5-11). The decoders are only ever created statically (Runtime/Unity/Decoders/DecoderRegistry.cs:417-425, new StbImageSharpDecoder() etc.) and resolved through the IImageDecoder/IAudioDecoder interfaces; there is no Type.GetType/Activator path, so the rules protect nothing. Decoders/ is 1,188 lines (DecoderRegistry 427, Aiff 255, Wav 225, stubs 176, rest 105), all kept with every member.

**Failure scenario.** An HTTP-only project (no textures, no audio, no TurboHTTP.Unity type referenced from its code) builds with Managed Stripping High: the merged link.xml names TurboHTTP.Unity, so UnityLinker processes the assembly instead of dropping it, keeps ~1.2k lines of decoder code plus DecoderRegistry's static state, and (because the assembly is now linked) keeps its RuntimeInitializeOnLoad hooks, see unity-design-02. The stubs tracked by #158 cannot even be stripped.

## Suggested fix
Delete Runtime/Unity/link.xml (the static new-expressions already root what is used) or reduce it to types that are genuinely reached by name. If some startup hook must survive stripping, put [Preserve] on that method instead of preserving unrelated types.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Runtime/Unity/link.xml is deleted or reduced to types actually reached by name; any startup hook that must survive stripping uses [Preserve].
- [ ] A Managed Stripping High build of an HTTP-only project no longer retains TurboHTTP.Unity decoder types (checked with the linker output or a stripping test).
- [ ] Texture and audio decoding still work in a stripped build; the change is paired with the unity-design-05 dependency.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails before the fix and passes after it or a Tests/Editor check that link.xml names only reflection-reached types.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `unity-design-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/unity.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Runtime/Unity/link.xml:3-12 preserves ten Decoders types with preserve="all". No reflection reaches them: rg for Type.GetType/Activator/GetTypes in Runtime/Unity, Runtime/Unity.WebSocket, Runtime/Bootstrap has no hit; decoders are created with new in DecoderRegistry.AddDefaultDecoders_NoLock (Decoders/DecoderRegistry.cs:417-425). Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:146-150 merges the file whenever TurboHTTP.Unity.dll is in the linker input (asmdef has no platform/define constraint), so UnityLinker is told to keep these types in every stripped build, including the #158 always-throwing stubs. File dates from the phase-15 commit d308f8e with no stated reason. #158 tracks the stubs, not the link.xml. The statically certain cost is ~1.2k lines of unstrippable decoder code; that naming the assembly also keeps its RuntimeInitializeOnLoad hooks alive in projects that reference no TurboHTTP.Unity type is UnityLinker behaviour (consistent with Runtime/Bootstrap/AssemblyInfo.cs:6-8) and only matters at stripping Low or above. Removing the file must be paired with unity-design-05, which currently depends on it.

Related: #35, #158.
